questions.help:
Road traffic collisions      
     
2 Road traffic collisions can be avoided  
2.3 The key: Reducing the risk
It is also possible to avoid many of the risk factors that are connected with the vehicle, the road or the environment.
In many collisions, the driver claims that the vehicle or road was an associated or main factor but the simple truth is that the driver could have behaved in a different way that would have avoided a collision. For example, if the driver had realised that the tyres were defective (by maintenance and inspection) they could have avoided the puncture (blow out) or if they had adopted an adequate speed and a safe distance when driving in the rain or snow, they could have avoided running into the vehicle ahead of them.
Proper maintenance and responsible driving reduces the chances that a “vehicle factor” or a “road factor” will be a cause of a collision.
(Página 250 del manual 'Learning to drive')

ILLNESS AND MEDICATION  
   
19 The consequences of illnesses and drugs in traffic collisions
To drive a vehicle requires certain conditions relating to the physical and mental aptitude of the driver to be initially satisfied and thereafter maintained. It is therefore necessary to go to a designated medical centre for drivers who will verify whether there is a serious impediment to the applicant or driver, which will prevent them performing this task safely.
A mild illness does not have to exclude driving, although it can reduce the ability to drive safely (for example, a common cold can cause sleepiness and loss of concentration). Therefore, you should always ask your doctor about the precautions to be taken before driving, especially if you have a chronic illness.
(Página 46 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
8 Speed limits are a necessity
 
Speed limits are not capricious. There are numerous factors that determine the implementation of a certain speed limit being imposed, (for example; the designated speed, the acceptable degree of congestion, the demands of existing traffic, etc.) The aim of a set speed limit is to allow vehicles to travel with the maximum guarantee of safety and fluidity.
One of the most important criteria is the designated speed of the road (the maximum safe speed that can be maintained on a section of road under favourable conditions). This means that a road is designated to be used at a certain generic or specific speed limit and traffic is not allowed to do a higher speed than that specified. To do otherwise means that safety will be compromised.
(Página 177 del manual 'Learning to drive')

In addition, the seat belt keeps the person inside the protective cell.
(Many people are killed each year when they are catapulted from their vehicle having not worn a seat belt). The seat belt is useful for all kinds of collisions however, not just front impacts.
With the use of seat belt, deaths caused by road traffic collisions have dropped significantly. It is estimated that by being properly secured in a vehicle there is a reduction, of nearly a half, of the likelihood of being killed in a road traffic collision.

4.2 Undertaking the manoeuvre
After checking that the manoeuvre can be commenced safely and also correctly signalling the manoeuvre, the driver must:
Move sideways at the correct time –tart the side movement at a sufficient distance from the hazard or other reason that motivated this change of course.
Carry the manoeuvre out progressively and gradually.
Undertake the manoeuvre without hindering other vehicles that is vehicles that are travelling in either direction. Be cautious when the manoeuvre involves entering into another lane including the lane where vehicle are travelling in the opposite direction (2 way traffic flow).
(Página 185 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
Road traffic collisions      
     
8 The rule - PAH
8.1 Protect: Measures to restore traffic safety
The driver of a vehicle, meaning those involved and those who are not, should comply with the following steps:
Most importantly, stay calm.
Stop and park - as soon as possible (if applicable) and in a manner that won’ create any danger to other traffic. This means, off the road, if possible and leaving the way clear for emergency vehicles. Turn off the engine, cut the ignition and apply the parking brake and turn on the emergency lights (hazard warning lights).
(Página 258 del manual 'Learning to drive')
